Three categories — `security-boundary-ownership` (8), `maintenance-burden` (7) and `bunny-visual-policy-independence` (5) — carry no runtime gate in the shared contract, because they are architectural judgements rather than things a harness can execute. They score zero here rather than being redistributed across the measurable categories, so the maximum a purely measured arm can currently reach is 80. Inflating an arm to 100 by spreading unmeasurable weight over measured gates would be the same error as calling `NOT_RUN` a pass.
